It is the oldest of the six paradigms in the [taxonomy](/world-models/taxonomy/): Embed to Control learned locally linear latent dynamics from raw images in 2015 . Drag "How far ahead to imagine" in the figure and the imagined throw peels away from the real one. In measured models, compounding error is shaped most by the system's own dynamics .
## Agents trained inside a recurrent latent model reached human-level Atari Ha and Schmidhuber trained an agent "entirely inside of its own hallucinated dream" and transferred it back to the real environment . PlaNet planned from pixels with deterministic and stochastic latent transitions . DreamerV3's Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM) pairs a recurrent state that carries memory with a stochastic categorical representation, and learns to reconstruct inputs and predict reward and continuation . Dreamer's actor and critic are trained purely on imagined latent rollouts from real encoded states, backpropagating value gradients through the model . DreamerV2, which added discrete latents, was the first agent to reach human-level performance on the 55-task Atari benchmark by learning inside a separately trained world model . ## DreamerV3: one recipe across 150 tasks DreamerV3 was evaluated on more than 150 tasks across eight domains with fixed hyperparameters. It uses symlog transforms for vector observations, free bits with KL balancing and percentile-based return normalization . In the 2025 Nature article its authors call it, to their knowledge, the first algorithm to collect diamonds in Minecraft from scratch without human data or adaptive curricula . Its MineRL-based task used abstract crafting actions, accelerated block breaking and sparse intermediate rewards for 12 milestones from log to diamond . DreamerV3 learned online; in 2025 Dreamer 4 became "the first agent to obtain diamonds in Minecraft purely from offline data", with a world model that runs in real time on a single GPU . ## TD-MPC2 drops the decoder and plans at every step MuZero planned with a model predicting only "the reward, the action-selection policy, and the value function" , and value-equivalence theory holds that capacity is "better used to build models that are directly useful for value-based planning" . TD-MPC trains reward, TD value and latent-state consistency predictions without reconstructing observations, and at each step runs short-horizon MPPI with a learned terminal value . TD-MPC2 keeps this planner, adds candidate sequences from a policy prior and warm-starts from the previous solution. The multitask experiment trained one 317M-parameter agent on 545M transitions from 240 single-task agents. This offline 80-task experiment is separate from the 104-task online benchmark, and aggregate normalized scores rose across five model sizes . MuDreamer replaced Dreamer's reconstruction with value and action prediction . ## DayDreamer taught a real quadruped to walk in about an hour DayDreamer builds on DreamerV2 and learns online without a simulator on four robots with shared hyperparameters. After about one hour of real training, a Unitree A1 learned to roll off its back, stand and walk, with manual repositioning at the area boundary that left its joints and orientation unchanged. SAC learned to roll over but neither stood nor walked within that budget . ## Latent models imagine only 3 to 16 steps ahead The 2023 DreamerV3 preprint lists imagination horizon H = 15 in a table and prediction horizon T = 16 in its actor-critic section, the 2024 revision keeps both labels, and the 2025 Nature article uses T = 16 . TD-MPC2 plans with H = 3 and bootstraps beyond it with a terminal value . DayDreamer states H = 16 in its methods and H = 15 in its appendix . MBPO keeps model rollouts short and "branched from real data" , and STEVE varies the horizon per example to limit model error . HWM, with world models at several time scales in one latent space, lifted real Franka pick-and-place from 0% to 70% . A 350M-parameter model trained on 427 hours across 210 tasks still showed perceptual, action-marginalized and scene-diverging hallucinations . ## Simulation-trained world models now transfer to real legged robots Robotic World Model (RWM) predicts observations over long horizons under partial observability with a GRU that feeds its predictions back in. Policies trained with MBPO-PPO in simulation showed zero-shot transfer to ANYmal D and Unitree G1, including under external disturbances; safe online hardware learning remains open . RWM-U adds uncertainty and trains policies "entirely from offline datasets" for a real quadruped and humanoid . SimDist pretrains in simulation and on hardware updates only the latent dynamics; on contact-rich manipulation and quadruped locomotion it kept improving where prior adaptation methods stalled or degraded . ## Refinements to latent planning bring uneven gains Dream-MPC refines policy-proposed action sequences by gradient ascent on predicted return, with an uncertainty penalty. Used in place of MPPI in pretrained TD-MPC2 and BMPC on 24 simulated tasks, over three seeds and ten episodes, the BMPC variant raises interquartile mean by 26.7% and mean by 20.5%. The TD-MPC2 variant beats its policy alone but does not consistently match MPPI . BMPC learns its policy by imitating the MPC planner , and HumanoidBench, one of the three task suites, poses whole-body humanoid tasks . TD-M(PC)² found that planner-generated data causes "persistent value overestimation" and fixed it with a policy constraint, gaining most on 61-DoF humanoids . Fast-WAM, a video world-action model, keeps video co-training but encodes the current frame once and runs action denoising on a chunk, with success similar to its imagine-then-execute variants on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0. On Galaxea R1 Lite towel folding it reports 190 ms inference latency against 810 ms for Fast-WAM-IDM on one RTX 5090D V2 32GB GPU . ## TD-MPC2's authors expect broad generalization to need far more tasks TD-MPC2's authors expect broad generalization, such as transfer to new embodiments, "will likely require several orders of magnitude more tasks" . In November 2025 the same group's Newt trained one language-conditioned world model jointly across 200 tasks . In simulation, one world model trained on up to 90 insertion tasks reached 56% zero-shot success on unseen parts, against 7% for a model-free baseline . DayDreamer's authors report that long hardware training causes wear needing human intervention or repair . ## Imagination tolerates slow models; online planning needs predictable latency Imagination-only training, as in Dreamer, tolerates slow generation but can bias the policy silently. Online planning, as in TD-MPC2, needs predictable latency and a fallback, and a planner that never changes its policy prior's proposal pays model cost for nothing. A latent model can also supply a representation: a simulation-trained world model predicted real legged-locomotion trajectories well enough to inform a separate controller . See the [model-based](/world-models/model-based-robot-learning/) and [evaluation](/world-models/evaluation/) guides.

Model-based robot learning is the family of methods that learn how the world responds to actions and use that model to plan, to train a policy in imagination, or both. Its two steps are learning a dynamics model and integrating planning with learning <Cite id="mbrl-survey-2020" />.

<Image id="daydreamer-a1-rollover-2022" />

The loop predicts futures under candidate actions, scores them, acts, observes the real transition and updates the model. Sutton proposed integrated architectures for learning, planning and reacting in 1990 <Cite id="dyna-1990" />.

<ModelBasedLoop className="my-6" />

<SelfCheck

  options={[

<span id="the-model-based-decomposition" />
## Model-based means predicting the effect of an action

A 2026 survey defines a world model as "an action-conditioned predictive system" <Cite id="manip-wm-survey-2026" />. Classical model-predictive control (MPC) uses explicit dynamics, such as MuJoCo's rigid-body and contact model <Cite id="mujoco-2012" />; model-based learning fits some or all of that transition to data.

A <Term id="world-model">world model</Term> need not predict pixels: value-equivalent models predict only what planning needs, "without compromising performance" <Cite id="value-equivalence-2020" />.

<span id="two-ways-to-use-imagined-experience" />
## A model can plan each step or train a policy in imagination

A planner rolls sampled action sequences through the model, executes the best first action and replans, so a new goal or cost needs no retraining, at the price of many rollouts per real step ([reward design and MPC](/rl-sim2real/reward-design-mpc/)). In 2016 Finn and Levine combined action-conditioned video prediction with MPC so a real robot could push novel objects <Cite id="deep-visual-foresight-2016" />. TD-MPC2 trained one 317M-parameter agent on 80 tasks <Cite id="tdmpc2-2023" />, and PointWorld, trained on about 2 million trajectories, plans with MPC at 0.1 s per inference on a real Franka without demonstrations <Cite id="pointworld-2026" />.

Dreamer instead trains a policy on trajectories imagined in a learned latent space <Cite id="dreamer-2019" />, and DreamerV3 covers more than 150 tasks with one configuration <Cite id="dreamerv3-2023" />. Dreamer 4 learns purely offline, a setting its authors tie to robotics, where interaction "can be unsafe and slow" <Cite id="dreamer4-2025" />. [Latent dynamics](/world-models/latent-dynamics/) covers these agents.

<span id="uncertainty-aware-models" />
## Uncertainty estimates keep policies from exploiting model errors

A policy trained on a model "tends to exploit regions where insufficient data is available", which ME-TRPO counters with an ensemble <Cite id="me-trpo-2018" />. PETS, a probabilistic ensemble, matches model-free asymptotic performance with 8 and 125 times fewer samples than SAC and PPO on half-cheetah <Cite id="pets-2018" />. MBPO keeps rollouts short and "branched from real data" <Cite id="mbpo-2019" />. In [offline RL](/rl-sim2real/offline-rl/), MOPO penalizes reward by model uncertainty <Cite id="mopo-2020" />.

<span id="why-physical-robots-make-the-model-harder" />
## Robots see only part of the state, yet learn useful models in minutes to hours

A robot observation is partial: cameras miss forces, friction and compliance, and RGBD gave an 80% improvement in fabric-folding success over RGB <Cite id="visuospatial-foresight-2020" />. Data is narrow too: Hansen and Wang call world-model hallucination "inherently a data coverage issue" and adapt a model to unseen simulated environments with 50 trajectories <Cite id="wm-hallucination-2026" />.

Chenyuan Zhou, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu and colleagues at Stanford and elsewhere (October 2026) condition a video world model on a 32-dimensional latent for hidden factors such as friction or mass, fitted at test time from one or two interactions while the model stays frozen <Cite id="t2z-2026" />. Averaged over four real-robot tasks, the adapted model's mean tracking error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels against the same model without a latent <Cite id="t2z-2026" />. Actions it picked succeeded 70.80% of the time against 26.47% for the model without a latent, though the paper does not state trial counts <Cite id="t2z-2026" />.

PDDM learned contact-rich manipulation on a 24-DoF hand from 4 real hours <Cite id="pddm-2019" />. DayDreamer ran Dreamer online on 4 robots without simulators; a quadruped learned to stand up and walk in 1 hour <Cite id="daydreamer-2022" />. SSRL adds a learned force ensemble to known Lagrangian dynamics and learned Go1 gaits from a few minutes of data <Cite id="ssrl-2024" />.

In September 2026, Claudio Canales, Marco Hutter and colleagues learned a probabilistic dynamics ensemble from scratch on an 11.5-ton hydraulic excavator. After 20 minutes, their sampling-based MPC tracked comparably to learned controllers trained on 100 to 150 minutes; after 40 it held sub-centimeter mean path error at high speed <Cite id="excavator-mbrl-2026" />. Hansen, Fox and colleagues trained one TD-MPC2 model in simulation on up to 90 insertion tasks, with 56% zero-shot success on unseen objects against 7% model-free <Cite id="insertion-world-models-2026" />.

<ExcavatorPractice className="my-6" />

## Model error is task-weighted

A two-millimeter error is irrelevant in free space and decisive at a tight connector. One-step prediction likelihood "is not always correlated with control performance", and task-effective models "do not necessarily need to be globally accurate" <Cite id="objective-mismatch-2020" />. The 2026 robot world-model survey stresses action-conditioned consistency and functional-utility evaluation <Cite id="world-model-survey-2026" />; the [evaluation guide](/world-models/evaluation/) gives a protocol.

<span id="neural-simulators-and-hybrid-models" />
## Neural and hybrid simulators now train real-robot policies

Robotic World Model trains a neural-network simulator for policy optimization <Cite id="robotic-world-model-2025" />, and RWM-U adds epistemic uncertainty to train real quadruped and humanoid policies entirely offline <Cite id="rwm-u-2025" />. RISE improves a VLA inside a [video world model](/world-models/generative-video/) scored by a progress-value model, gaining 35 to 45 points on three real tasks <Cite id="rise-2026" />.

Hybrids keep known physics and learn what it misses: TossingBot learns residuals on a physics-based throw and reached 500+ mean picks per hour <Cite id="tossingbot-2019" />, and ASAP fits a delta action model to real Unitree G1 data <Cite id="asap-2025" />. ## Model-based means predicting the effect of an action

A 2026 survey defines a world model as "an action-conditioned predictive system" <Cite id="manip-wm-survey-2026" />. A planner rolls sampled action sequences through the model, executes the best first action and replans, so a new goal or cost needs no retraining, at the price of many rollouts per real step ([reward design and MPC](/rl-sim2real/reward-design-mpc/)). ## They solve different specification problems

MuJoCo models articulated bodies, constraints and contact with explicit equations and parameters <Cite id="mujoco-2012" />. Isaac Lab wraps GPU simulation, sensors, task definitions and batched environments into a robot-learning workflow <Cite id="isaac-lab-2025" />. Disney Research, Google DeepMind and NVIDIA gave their Newton GPU engine to the Linux Foundation in September 2025 <Cite id="newton-lf-2025" />. NVIDIA reports that MuJoCo Warp speeds up MJX by 252x on locomotion and 475x on manipulation on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU <Cite id="newton-manipulation-blog-2026" />.

A learned world model estimates transitions from observations and actions, often in a latent or video space, and trades parameter error for dataset and generalization error. Hansen and Wang call hallucination "inherently a data coverage issue" <Cite id="wm-hallucination-2026" />. A 2026 survey lists simulation among a world model's roles, with planning, policy learning, evaluation and data generation <Cite id="world-model-survey-2026" />.

## Comparison by engineering property

<SimVsModelTable className="my-6" />

<span id="what-each-representation-costs-to-run" />
## A latent planner needs seconds per action, a video planner minutes

The table compares the query cost of four representations on one machine; the FLOP row is a derived order-of-magnitude estimate. For a physics baseline, Isaac Gym steps thousands of environments in parallel on one GPU and trained robot tasks 2 to 3 orders of magnitude faster than CPU-simulator pipelines <Cite id="isaac-gym-2021" />.

<WorldModelCostTable className="my-6" />

As the decode reference, Llama 3 8B <Cite id="llama-3-2024" /> holds about 16 GB of fp16 weights. Its 32 layers and 8 grouped-query key-value heads <Cite id="llama-3-herd-2024" /> give a KV cache of about 128 KB per token.

In the latent column, V-JEPA 2-AC's cross-entropy planner takes about 16 seconds per action with 800 samples over 10 iterations. A Cosmos video planner took about 4 minutes with 80 samples, roughly 15x slower, and both looked one step ahead <Cite id="vjepa2-2025" />. LeWorldModel plans up to 48x faster than foundation-model world models <Cite id="leworldmodel-2026" />.

<WorldModelOutputTimes className="my-6" />

## Clip generators run far slower than interactive world models

In the costlier video column, Cosmos Predict1 spans diffusion models at 7B to 14B and autoregressive models at 4B to 13B <Cite id="cosmos-predict-2025" />. NVIDIA measured Predict2's 14B Video2World at 56 GB of VRAM and about 85 seconds per 480p clip on a GB200, over 30 minutes on a DGX Spark <Cite id="cosmos-predict2-perf-2025" />. The Predict1 14B card lists over 80 GB for a five-second 1280x704 clip with the prompt upsampler offloaded <Cite id="cosmos-1-diffusion-14b-card-2025" />. Such offline clip generators cannot serve as 24 fps runtimes, and a policy calling one per action step inherits their latency.

## Gaussian splats render in milliseconds but carry no dynamics

3D Gaussian Splatting renders rasterizable primitives in tens of milliseconds or less per frame, with no weights or tokens, and stores the scene as an asset of 1 to 5 million Gaussians <Cite id="3dgs-2023" />. A splat shows what a view looks like; physics must say what an action does.

<Image id="gaussian-splatting-garden-2023" />

<span id="where-physics-remains-difficult-to-replace" />
## Physics stays ahead for untried actions and checkable safety limits

Planning, as in [model-based RL](/world-models/model-based-robot-learning/), queries actions the dataset did not take. A physics engine integrates them while its modeled regime holds; a learned model must extrapolate, and a planner can exploit its errors by picking actions with spuriously high predicted reward. Across six video generators, physical understanding was "severely limited, and unrelated to visual realism" <Cite id="physics-iq-2025" />. Safety constraints also favor explicit state: joint limits, collision geometry, force bounds and signed distances can be checked directly, while a predicted video may imply a collision without the quantity a monitor needs.

<PlannerExploit className="my-6" />

<span id="where-learning-has-the-advantage" />
## Learning captures appearance and contact that are costly to model

A learned visual model can absorb from video the textures, reflections, cables and clutter that are expensive to render; deformable contacts, unmodeled actuators and wear also resist parameterization. Robotic World Model aims a neural simulator at policy optimization <Cite id="robotic-world-model-2025" />, and RoboWorld at policy evaluation, with task-progress scoring and rankings validated against real robots <Cite id="roboworld-2026" />.

<span id="three-hybrid-patterns" />
## Four hybrid patterns

### Learn appearance, keep dynamics

Real-to-sim systems reconstruct a scene's appearance and keep a physics engine for motion and contact, as RoboGSim does with Gaussian splatting <Cite id="robogsim-2024" />. SplatSim's splat-rendered simulator gave zero-shot RGB policies 86.25% success, against 97.5% when trained on real data <Cite id="splatsim-2024" />. PhysTwin extends it to deformables, building spring-mass twins of ropes, stuffed animals, cloth and delivery packages from videos and rendering them with Gaussian splats <Cite id="phystwin-2025" />.

### Generate content, keep the engine

[Generative simulation](/world-models/generative-sim/) uses models to author objects, layouts, tasks and assets inside a physics engine, so the generator supplies coverage while the engine keeps contact causal. RoboCasa supplies large-scale everyday manipulation environments <Cite id="robocasa-2024" />, and RoboCasa365 extends it to training and benchmarking generalist robots <Cite id="robocasa365-2026" />.

### Learn residual dynamics

Residual models start from explicit dynamics and learn the measured difference, such as actuator delay or contact impulses. With a named error to fit, this is the most conservative hybrid <Cite id="hwangbo-2019" />. ASAP trains a delta action model on real Unitree G1 data and beats system-identification, domain-randomization and delta-dynamics baselines on tracking error <Cite id="asap-2025" />. A residual fitted to nominal walking may still fail on a fall.

### Pretrain in simulation, adapt dynamics on hardware

SimDist trains a world model on simulated experience, then on real data updates only the latent dynamics, keeping the encoder, reward model and value function. Its authors say this reduces adaptation to supervised system identification, and it kept improving with experience on contact-rich manipulation and quadruped locomotion <Cite id="simdist-2026" />.

Both simulator types can be wrong in correlated ways: a policy may exploit contact softness in physics or visual shortcuts in a world model. SIMPLER builds matched environments and correlates simulated with real policy performance <Cite id="simpler-2024" />. Apply that test to both types with several policy families and held-out environments, scored on the same real outcome ([world-model evaluation](/world-models/evaluation/)).

<Image id="isaac-lab-assembly-real-2025" />

<span id="a-selection-rule" />
## Choose by what can be specified and what the data cover

Use explicit physics when state and mechanics can be specified, counterfactuals are broad, constraints need inspection or parallel stepping matters most ([parallel simulation for RL](/rl-sim2real/parallel-sim-rl/)). Use a learned world model when real observations hold structure that is costly to author, data cover the decisions of interest and validation can anchor model error. Use a hybrid for a localized mismatch, as ANYmal's simulator did <Cite id="hwangbo-2019" />; [classical control](/classical/control/) and [latent dynamics](/world-models/latent-dynamics/) cover the two ends.
